EGFR.role: Keratinocyte proliferation and epidermal barrier homeostasis
EGFR.logic: EGFR is a receptor tyrosine kinase highly expressed in basal keratinocytes and the outer root sheath of hair follicles, where its signaling through the downstream MAPK cascade sustains keratinocyte proliferation, differentiation, and migration and maintains epidermal barrier integrity. Blockade of its tyrosine-kinase activity suppresses this signaling, alters keratinocyte differentiation, upregulates pro-inflammatory chemokines, and drives an inflammatory infiltrate into the epidermis and follicles, along with impaired barrier function and follicular inflammation.

COX2.role: Prostaglandin synthesis in arachidonic acid metabolism
COX2.logic: COX-2 (PTGS2) is an inducible cyclooxygenase that, together with the constitutive COX-1, oxygenates arachidonic acid to prostaglandin H2, the precursor of prostaglandins including prostaglandin E2; the two isoforms share a highly conserved catalytic site. Reduced cyclooxygenase activity lowers prostaglandin E2 and diverts arachidonic acid toward cysteinyl leukotriene formation. Elevated cysteinyl leukotrienes increase vascular permeability and promote mast-cell degranulation, contributing to urticaria and angioedema.

MEK1.role: MAPK cascade signal transduction in keratinocytes
MEK1.logic: MEK1 (MAP2K1) is a dual-specificity kinase acting downstream of RAS and RAF in the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade, where it phosphorylates and activates ERK to relay EGFR-initiated signals that sustain keratinocyte proliferation, differentiation, and follicular homeostasis. Inhibition of its kinase activity suppresses ERK signaling in the epidermis, disrupting keratinocyte differentiation, upregulating inflammatory chemokines, and recruiting a follicular inflammatory infiltrate, paralleling the epidermal effects of EGFR blockade.

BRAF.role: MAPK cascade signaling and paradoxical pathway activation in keratinocytes
BRAF.logic: BRAF is a serine/threonine kinase relaying RAS signals to MEK and ERK in the MAPK cascade. In keratinocytes carrying wild-type BRAF, ATP-competitive BRAF inhibitors paradoxically activate this pathway: the drug-bound protomer transactivates its partner within RAS-dependent RAF dimers, amplifying ERK output. When an upstream activating RAS mutation is already present, this elevated ERK signaling drives keratinocyte hyperproliferation and neoplastic lesions such as keratoacanthoma and cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma.

pathway_rules: In basal keratinocytes and hair follicles, EGFR signaling maintains proliferation, differentiation, and barrier homeostasis; loss of its tyrosine-kinase activity suppresses the downstream MAPK cascade, disrupts differentiation, upregulates chemokines, and recruits inflammatory infiltrate, producing papulopustular (acneiform) rash, xerosis, and paronychia.

MEK1 lies downstream of EGFR in the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade; inhibition of MEK1 suppresses ERK signaling in keratinocytes and reproduces the epidermal consequences of EGFR blockade, likewise driving papulopustular rash, xerosis, and periungual inflammation.

In keratinocytes with wild-type BRAF, BRAF inhibitors paradoxically activate the MAPK cascade through RAF dimer transactivation, and in cells bearing a pre-existing RAS mutation this amplified ERK signaling promotes keratinocyte hyperproliferation, manifesting as verrucal keratosis, keratoacanthoma, and cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma.

Cyclooxygenase inhibition lowers prostaglandin E2 and shifts arachidonic acid toward cysteinyl leukotriene production; the elevated leukotrienes raise vascular permeability and promote mast-cell degranulation, driving cross-reactive urticaria and angioedema across chemically diverse cyclooxygenase inhibitors.
